findings.shape: Original fir branching hierarchy, selected two-ranked flattened needle cues with pale lower bands, greyer continuous bark and upright narrow bracted cone studies. Cone-bearing upper shoot cues are more ascending; foliage arrangement varies with shoot context.
findings.surface: Original grey continuous bark, flattened darker green needle surfaces with pale lower-band cues and upright bracted woody cone studies. These are original numerical surfaces, not calibrated photographic textures.
findings.movement: The same trunk, branches, leaves and cones remain present. Working sway is small authored external branch deflection with anchored roots; no wind, stiffness, damping or physiological solver. Full cone maturation/release is explicitly unavailable. Full germination and organ-by-organ seed-to-tree development remain unavailable; the adult crown is not resized into a false developmental sequence.

corrections: Replaced the generic sparse pine-like draft with a distinct fir architecture, selected two-ranked flattened needle cues and upright cones.
Separated pale underside-band cues from the darker leaf base colour and added partial rounded/notched tips.
Narrowed overlapping leaf surfaces, reduced the excessive pale blend and warmed small woody shoots after actual close-view defects were found.
Added ascending upper-shoot cues and grey bark; kept cone disintegration unavailable instead of substituting pine-style opening.
Added retained branch support and separate anatomy focus.
findings.residual: The whole crown retains conspicuous regular tiering and bright needle-edge aliasing in some views. Fine leaf tips, stomatal bands, bark relief and bract/scale anatomy remain idealized. Cone disintegration, seed release, measured foliage optics and a complete seed-to-tree developmental sequence remain unavailable.
